summary: Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned an MA from the University of Mumbai (by 1919) and a PhD from Harvard (~1929-1932). He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Purushottama Bilimoria works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed his PhD at La Trobe University. He has held positions at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, Stony Brook, Columbia, and UC Berkeley.

Pushpendra Kumar is an Indologist who studied under Satyavrat Shastri. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (attested 1976) and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon was active in Indology and other fields. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and was President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London in 2014. Kyaw also served as a postdoctoral research fellow at King's College London (attested 2017).

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and completed his PhD at Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts at Oxford, All Souls College, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Qian Lin is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Fudan, Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD 2015). Lin studied under Rupert Gethin, Richard Salomon, and doctoral supervisor Collett Cox, among others.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who completed doctoral studies under Wu Hung and Irene Winter. Ning worked as a researcher at Dunhuang Academy and taught at San Diego State, Yale, and Michigan.

Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Xuehai Tang, National Tsing Hua University, and under Kang Youwei, he held posts at Current Affairs Academy, the Translation Bureau, Nankai, Tsinghua, and the National Library of China.

Qing Duan worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University and earning a PhD at Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, Duan served as a professor at Peking University (~1987-2022).

Qingying Chen was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Qinghai Nationalities University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University under Wang Yao. Chen worked at Delingha High School, Qinghai Nationalities University, Minzu, Qinghai ASS, and China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Zhu has held professorial posts at Peking University (attested 2004) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

R. Balasubramanian was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from approximately 1975 to 1990.
R. D. Vadekar was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).

R. Gordon Wasson studied at Columbia and LSE. He worked in journalism, served with the American Expeditionary Forces, was on the American Council of Learned Societies Executive Committee, and worked at Guaranty Trust Company and J.P. Morgan & Co.

R. H. Tawney was an English historian who studied at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1899-1903). He taught at the University of Glasgow (~1906-1908) and was on the faculty at the London School of Economics (~1913-1949).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1958).
R. P. Paranjpye was a student of Vaman Shivram Apte. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).
